newsitem.title: CHINA: China explains conviction of princeling.
newsitem.headline: China explains conviction of princeling.

text.p: Disgraced Chinese tycoon Zhou Beifang, a son of one of China's top families, was treated leniently and given only a suspended death sentence because he chose to confess, state media said on Thursday.
"According to Zhou's case, he was not a criminal who must be executed immediately," the Workers' Daily said, quoting an official of the Beijing Municipal Higher People's Court.

The court showed leniency to Zhou, former chairman of Hong Kong-listed affiliates of the giant state-owned Capital Iron and Steel Corp (Shougang), becuase he confessed voluntarily and showed remorse, the official said.

During the investigation, Zhou confessed to accepting bribes totalling HK$9.28 million (US$1.2 million) even before prosecutors obtained evidence against him. He helped them to recover HK$6.4 million ($820,000), the official said.
Zhou also voluntarily confessed to paying 1.2 million yuan ($144,600) in bribes to three people, including two former officials of the Beijing city government, he said.
Zhou's death sentence was suspended for two years. Such suspensions usually mean the sentence will not be carried out if the prisoner repents and cooperates with the authorities.
Zhou is one of China's so-called "princelings", or children of the ruling party elite, who enjoy wide influence due to their top level connections.
